crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Finding Acquisition Targets
children.blurb: Finding acquisition targets in private equity and deal sourcing means identifying companies that fit a fund's thesis, size, sector and value creation plan.

children.name: Data Room Diligence
children.blurb: Data room diligence is the structured review of documents that a target company places in a secure virtual data room during a private equity or merger and acquisition process.

children.name: Buyout Modelling
children.blurb: Buyout modelling is the quantitative representation of a leveraged acquisition, covering sources and uses of funds, debt tranches, cash flow sweeps, exit assumptions, and returns such as internal rate of return and multiple of invested capital.

children.name: Private Market Valuation
children.blurb: Private market valuation is the practice of estimating what a private company or a private asset is worth when no public market price exists.

children.name: Tracking Synergies After a Merger
children.blurb: Tracking synergies after a merger means measuring whether the combined company performs better than the standalone businesses would have, across cost, revenue, and capital efficiency.

sections.body: Private equity and deal sourcing is the work of finding companies to buy, checking whether they are worth the price, building the financing case, and measuring what changes after the deal closes. AI now reads filings, news, company websites, financial statements, contracts, and customer records to flag possible targets, extract terms, compare peers, and draft parts of a model. It also scans data rooms for clauses, obligations, and anomalies that a human team might miss under time pressure. The site tracks 357 merger and acquisition filings, which gives a concrete base for studying how deals are announced and structured. This is not a theoretical exercise, because deal teams already use software to sort thousands of documents and rank candidates before anyone speaks to a founder or banker.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is strongest where the inputs are text heavy and the output can be checked, such as document review, data extraction, target screening, and comparable company analysis. It is weaker where the question requires judgment about people, strategy, or a negotiated price with little public data. Private company valuation remains hard because private firms disclose less, report on different schedules, and often have no clean market comparable. Synergy estimates are also uncertain, since cost cuts and revenue gains depend on integration choices that happen after the deal. AI can speed up the first pass, but it does not remove the need for human review, confidentiality controls, and investment committee judgment. The honest limit is that a model can be precise about a document and still be wrong about a business.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: Finding Acquisition Targets is the entry point for sourcing, showing how AI builds candidate lists from filings, news, and company data. Data Room Diligence then covers how models read contracts, financial records, and legal documents to surface risks and open questions. Buyout Modelling looks at debt capacity, cash flow projections, and return scenarios that shape a bid. Private Market Valuation addresses the harder problem of pricing a company that has no daily market price. Tracking Synergies After a Merger follows the deal after close, measuring cost and revenue effects against the original thesis. Read together, these pages trace the deal lifecycle from first screen to post-close review.
